title: Peripheral arterial disease
summary: Peripheral arterial disease (as determined by appropriate medically acceptable imaging per 4.00A3d, 4.00G2, 4.00G5, 4.00G6) causing intermittent claudication (see 4.00G1), meeting one of: A resting ankle/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio less than 0.50; B decrease in systolic blood pressure at the ankle on exercise of 50% or more of pre-exercise level requiring ≥10 minutes to return to pre-exercise level (see 4.00G7a, 4.00C16-4.00C17); C resting toe systolic pressure less than 30 mm Hg (see 4.00G7c, 4.00G8); or D resting toe/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio less than 0.40 (see 4.00G7c).

children.criterion: Peripheral arterial disease, as determined by appropriate medically acceptable imaging (see 4.00A3d, 4.00G2, 4.00G5, and 4.00G6), causing intermittent claudication (see 4.00G1)
One of A, B, C, or D
Resting ankle/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio of less than 0.50

Decrease in systolic blood pressure at the ankle on exercise (see 4.00G7a and 4.00C16-4.00C17) of 50 percent or more of pre-exercise level and requiring 10 minutes or more to return to pre-exercise level
Resting toe systolic pressure of less than 30 mm Hg (see 4.00G7c and 4.00G8)
Resting toe/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio of less than 0.40 (see 4.00G7c)
